summary: Local baseline built from the host's own Windows files, merged with the nearest shipped baselines in a BaselineView with four trust levels (Exact, Merged, Local, None). Presence may come from any set; absence below Exact is 'inferred' and capped: soft blocker BaselineInferred, seal check, policy rule P-BL-1. Never Safe, never preselected. Design text: docs/BASELINE_LOCAL_DESIGN.md.
model_routing: critical: Fable medium, or Opus high with a Fable review; high: Opus high; medium: Opus medium; gates: scripts under a Haiku babysitter, judged in review.
invariants: L1 Additive sources: every source and neighbour only adds to 'Windows' own'; nothing is subtracted at hash level.
L2 Complete or unused: an incomplete local baseline is used for presence only.
L3 Exact is untouched: with an exact shipped baseline the plans are byte-identical to the M1b gate plans; the local baseline is not built or read.
L4 The cap: absence below Exact never yields Safe and never preselects.

L5 Monotone: a view below Exact only takes away. Every item offered below Exact has an item of the no-baseline result with the same target (or, when there is none, a key or directory that contains it) whose band is at least as high (not listed < Blocked < Weak < Likely < Safe) and which is preselected if the item is. Nothing new is offered, no band is raised, preselected(non-exact) is a subset of preselected(none); what was Blocked is Blocked or no longer listed (the Blocked set is not a superset).
L6 A local file is never accepted as an exact baseline (header tag, directory, name).
L7 Advice only lowers a band.
budgets: Cold build, background priority, parallel: <= 30 s on the 591-program host, <= 120 s on a 2-vCPU VM. Phases baseline.local.list, .expand, .parse, .hive, .appx, .write.
Peak memory of the build <= 300 MB; cache file <= 15 MB.
Source-id check <= 0.3 s per engine start.
Warm load of the view (local + 2 neighbours) <= 1.5 s, <= 80 MB resident.
A scan never waits for the build: it runs with trust None and a warning.

packages.title: purge-win: expand WinSxS component manifests
packages.scope: Read feature only. find_base(): newest WinSxS\amd64_microsoft-windows-servicingstack_* directory, wcp.dll loaded as a data file, resource type 0x266 id 1. expand(bytes, base): 'DCM\x01' -> msdelta ApplyDeltaB(0, base, bytes[4..]), output freed with DeltaFree; plain XML returned as is; 'DCN\x01' (delta without a base) and 'DCS\x01' (LZMS) handled or reported as Unsupported with a count. list(): names, sizes and write times of WinSxS\Manifests in one directory pass.
rules: No write API, no process spawn. The base is read once per build.
A failed expansion is an error value per file, never a panic; the caller counts it (seal).
Output size cap per manifest 64 MB; larger is an error.
Document whether ApplyDeltaB is called from several threads; if the spike shows it is not safe, a mutex and the budget is re-measured.
tests: win-unit (real Windows): base found; 200 manifests expand to text starting with '<?xml'; a truncated DCM file is an error; a plain XML file passes through.
Unit: header detection for DCM, DCN, DCS, plain, empty.
packages.acceptance: win-unit passes on both rig VMs and the host; 0 failures over all manifests of the three machines, or every failure explained.

packages.title: purge-win: read-only offline hive walk
packages.scope: offreg.dll loaded from System32 by full path: OROpenHive on a file opened with shared read, OREnumKey, OREnumValue (names and types only), ORCloseHive. A walker that yields key paths and value names depth-first with caps (depth 64, 2,000,000 keys).
rules: Never RegLoadKey, RegLoadAppKey or any call that mounts the hive.
No ORSaveHive, no create or set call is bound.
Transaction logs are not replayed; the doc comment says so.
tests: win-unit: C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT opens unelevated and yields 'Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' or its parent; a missing file and a non-hive file are errors.
check-deps: the forbidden-identifier list gains the offreg write calls.
packages.acceptance: win-unit passes on both VMs and the host.

packages.title: Pure parser: component manifest to baseline records
packages.scope: parse(xml, &mut Records) -> ManifestStats. Streaming XML, elements matched by local name (registryKey and asm:registryKey alike). Mapping rules of design section 3.2: roots, ancestors, 32-bit view doubling for wow64 and x86, value names with hash 0, file and directory destinations through the macro table, unknown macros skipped and counted, publicKeyToken recorded in the stats.
rules: Pure: no I/O, no Windows call; runs on Linux CI.
Records are text (escaped as kb/baselines/README.md says); hashing happens only in the loader.
Never drops a key because another manifest version lacks it; the union over all files is the result.
Malformed XML is an error for that file; no partial records from it are kept.
No real Microsoft manifest is committed.
tests: Fixtures: HKCR CLSID with subkeys; asm: prefixed elements; HKEY_CURRENT_USER key (both spellings recorded); wow64 manifest (both views); key name with a known macro, with an unknown macro; file and directory with each macro; malformed XML; a manifest without registry keys.
Property: every recorded key's parent is recorded; records are a superset when a second manifest is added.
Round trip: records written to a file and loaded through the baseline normaliser answer has_key for every spelling the existing tests use (HKCR, WOW6432Node link, HKCU).
packages.acceptance: All tests pass; the macro list found on the three machines (BL-MEASURE) is covered or each gap is listed.

packages.title: Default hive, HKU\.DEFAULT and inbox package manifests to records
packages.scope: trait LocalSources { manifests() -> iterator of (name, bytes or error); default_hive() -> key and value-name walk; system_default() -> walk of HKU\.DEFAULT through RegistrySource; inbox_packages() -> (full name, AppxManifest.xml text, repository ProgIDs) }. hive.rs maps the default hive to HKU\S-1-5-21-0-0-0-1000\<path>. appx.rs parses file type, protocol, COM class, interface and ProgID declarations into Classes keys. Live implementation: purge-win sxs, offreg, appx. Inbox means signature kind System, or Microsoft-published and provisioned.
rules: Read only. Package directories are read file by file; WindowsApps is never listed.
A package whose manifest cannot be read is counted, not fatal (seal floor in BL-BUILD).
Third-party packages are never included: their keys are another app's, not Windows'.
tests: Fixture hive walk to records; SID placeholder check through the normaliser.
AppX manifest fixtures (hand-written): file type association, protocol, comServer, comInterface.
win-unit: live sources return non-empty data on a clean VM.
packages.acceptance: Tests pass; the spike note in the package report answers which repository values name generated AppX ProgIDs, or S4 is reduced to declared names.

packages.title: Local baseline build, seal, file format, reader, CLI
crates_files: crates/purge-index/src/baseline.rs (shared record parser made reusable; header handling unchanged)
bins/purge-engine/src/cli/args.rs, cli.rs (verbs baseline build, baseline info)
packages.scope: build(sources, os, opts) -> LocalBaselineFile: parallel expand and parse (rayon or scoped threads, background priority), de-duplicated sorted records, #src lines, completeness seal (design 3.4), header '#purge-baseline-local 1' with builder version and source id, '#end' line with record count and SHA-256. LocalBaseline::from_bytes reads it into the same hashed sets as Baseline and exposes complete(), sources(), id(). CLI: 'baseline build --out <file>' and 'baseline info <file>'.
rules: Baseline::from_bytes keeps refusing the local header; LocalBaseline::from_bytes refuses the shipped header (L6).
A file without a correct #end line, with another builder version, or over 64 MB is a miss, never partial data.
Output is deterministic for the same inputs (sorted, no times in the body) so two builds can be compared.
The CLI verb writes only the named output file.
tests: Fixture build: expected records, #src counts, deterministic bytes.
Seal: each floor violated in turn gives complete() = false with the reason; an unreadable source likewise.
Truncated file, wrong #end hash, swapped header tags: all misses.
Budget test (ignored by default, run on the rig): timing lines present.
packages.acceptance: Tests pass; 'baseline build' completes on both VMs and the host inside the budgets or the measured numbers are reported for gate M.

packages.title: rigtool baseline-diff, area table, replay with an injected view
crates_files: kb/baselines/view.json (new: areas with merged/local flags, neighbour limit)
packages.scope: baseline-diff as in design 8.1: per area and total: truth, covered local, covered merged, false absent local and merged, extra, per-source share, shared-container-shape count, first 200 false-absent keys per area; JSON report 'purge.baseline-diff/1'. Compares normalised text keys inside the capture scope only. Campaign scripts for R1, R2, R5.
rules: The diff works on names, not hashes.
Area matching is by normalised prefix and by leaf shape; the area list is data in view.json.
VM rig rules: clean snapshots only; official downloads only; nothing installed for R1 and R2.
tests: Synthetic truth, local and neighbour files with known counts per area.
Shape classifier unit tests (.ext, OpenWithProgids, shell, shellex, ProgID, vendor depth 1 and 2).
packages.acceptance: Self-test passes; R1 report is produced end to end by the script.

packages.title: Gate M: measure the local baseline on both VMs and the host
packages.scope: Runs R1, R2, R5 of design 8.2. Fills view.json: an area is marked merged when S2 holds for it on both VMs, local when S3 holds. Reports W1, W4 and the estimates of design 8.2 against the measured numbers. Decides: wave 4 starts (W1 met), or the feature ships presence-only, or S5 (INF) is added first.
rules: No engine behaviour changes before this gate passes review.
Every false-absent key of a shared-container shape is listed by name in the report, with the source that should have had it.
packages.acceptance: Report reviewed (Fable). W1: merged coverage >= 99.0% of truth keys in scope and >= 99.8% in merged areas on both VMs. S2 and S3 per area as in design 8.3. W4 budgets.

packages.title: BaselineView: trust levels, neighbour selection, areas
crates_files: crates/purge-kb or purge-index: reader of kb/baselines/view.json
packages.scope: BaselineTrust, BaselineView, Absence as in design 4.3. Constructors: exact(Baseline), merged(LocalBaseline, Vec<Baseline>, Areas), local(LocalBaseline, Areas), none(presence sets). select_neighbours(dir, os, limit) by the rule of design 4.1. P methods are unions; key_absent applies scope, areas and trust; exact_value answers only from Exact.
rules: Exact view: every method returns exactly what Baseline returns today (L3); the local baseline is not consulted.
key_absent never returns Proven below Exact and never returns Inferred for trust None, an incomplete local baseline, a key out of scope or an area not flagged.
has_key_exact_view on a union: present when any set has that very spelling or, for shared subtrees, the twin, as today per set.
No set difference, no negative cache (design section 6).
A neighbour whose header and name disagree is skipped with a warning, as an exact file would be.
tests: Truth table: trust x (in local, in neighbour, in scope, area flag) -> Absence.
Neighbour selection: same build other ubr; nearest below and above; limit 1000; tie on edition; at most three; none.
Exact view equals Baseline on the synthetic fixture for every public method.
Property: adding a set never turns Present into anything else.
Incomplete local baseline gives trust None and still answers presence.
packages.acceptance: Tests pass; Fable review of the truth table and the selection rule.

packages.title: Model and policy: BaselineInferred, P-BL-1, notes, templates, fingerprint field
packages.scope: Blocker::BaselineInferred (soft). PolicyCtx::baseline_trust. Rule P-BL-1 in decide: with Merged or Local and a RegKey target, evidence of an absence-dependent kind (ProvenOwnedSkeleton, ComKeyOwnership, HarvestedToken, key-scope InstallerManifest, key-scope ChainedRef) does not support Safe; Note::BaselineInferred. Explanation templates of design 4.4. POLICY_VERSION bump. Fingerprint field baseline_view {name, trust, local_id}; old fingerprints read as before.
rules: With trust Exact or None the decision of every existing golden row is unchanged.
The new blocker is soft in is_hard(), has a stable name and sort rank, and old plans still deserialize.
P-BL-1 holds without the blocker being present (backstop), and the blocker alone is enough (carrier).
Ai rule 7 is not touched.
tests: Golden rows: each absence-dependent kind x trust (Exact, Merged, Local, None) x blocker present or absent.
A RegKey with UninstallerArtifact or AppNamedKeyWithRootRef evidence stays Safe under Merged (not absence-dependent).
Explain: both templates; schema round trip of the fingerprint with and without the field.
packages.acceptance: Golden tests pass; replay with exact baselines byte-identical to the M1b gate plans apart from the policy version string.

packages.title: Scan and harvest: classify every baseline use as presence or absence
packages.scope: ScanCtx::baseline and the harvest contexts become &BaselineView. Every site is rewritten per the table of design 4.3. CandidateBuilder::absence adds the detail facts and the blocker. The seal in ctx.run refuses an absence-dependent RegKey candidate without the blocker when the view is below Exact. Fingerprint absence facts are read with min(harvest trust, scan trust). testkit::baseline returns an Exact view; a new testkit::merged_view. xtask baseline-sites.
rules: No site keeps a hand-written 'not has_key' test: absence is asked only through key_absent.
Unknown takes exactly today's no-baseline path at each site (X-SYSTIDY, Tier B, no token evidence).
restore_source uses exact_value only.
No new registry or file walk (no-new-walks stays green).
tests: Per A site: Inferred gives evidence + blocker + band Likely + not preselected; Unknown gives today's result; Proven gives today's exact result.
Golden cls_assoc_vscode_merged.txt; the existing baseline and no_baseline goldens unchanged.
Seal test: a candidate built without the blocker is dropped and reported.
L5 property test over the scanner test worlds, as L5 is stated in the invariants: nothing new offered, no band raised, preselected subset; per-scanner non-vacuity.
Existing tests named in design 4.6 pass unchanged in meaning.
packages.acceptance: cargo test, clippy, xtask check-deps, scanner-coverage, no-new-walks, baseline-sites all pass; Fable review of the site table against the code.

packages.title: Cache directory, source id, invalidation, pipeline wiring
crates_files: install/install.ps1 (only if the data root needs the subdirectory)
packages.scope: LocalCache::open(dir, fs): the DiskTableCache directory rule. source_id(sources). load(os, builder version, source id) -> Option<LocalBaseline>. store() through a temporary file and rename, only elevated, then removal of older files (keep two). Pipeline: exact match -> Exact view and nothing else happens; otherwise open the cache, start a background build when elevated and missing, select neighbours, build the view; warnings name the trust and the reason. When elevated, kb\baselines must be admin-only writable or no shipped baseline is used. PolicyCtx gets the view's trust. engine.hello reports baseline_trust beside baseline_available.
rules: Unelevated: read an accepted cache, never write, never build.
A cache directory that fails the rule is ignored (trust None), never repaired.
The build never blocks a scan; a scan that starts first runs with trust None and says so.
A fingerprint harvested with one view and scanned with another uses the weaker trust.
pipeline test baselines_are_only_used_for_an_exact_match stays as the test of the exact loader.
tests: Fixture file system: user-owned directory, inherited Users write ACE, reparse point, protected DACL: only the last is accepted.
Invalidation: new ubr, changed manifest directory stamp, changed package list, new builder version: each a miss; old files removed after a store.
Pipeline: exact host builds nothing and reads no cache (metered sources); unelevated without a cache gives None with the warning; elevated kb directory writable by Users gives no shipped baseline.
Crash safety: a temporary file left behind is ignored and removed.
packages.acceptance: Tests pass; Fable security review: can a standard user plant, poison, downgrade or delay the cache to gain a delete.

packages.title: Residue output and advice types (interface only)
packages.scope: Scan result carries the residue list of design section 7. Advice types with validation (lengths, enums, binding to scan_id, id, item_fp) and the mapping to Ai evidence: 'windows' negative, 'app' and 'unknown' note only. No reader of advice files, no model, no MCP tool: M6.
rules: No value data, no file content in the residue.
Advice can never add a candidate, remove a blocker, raise a band or preselect (unit-tested at the mapping).
Residue is capped (1,000 items) with a count of the rest.
tests: Schema round trips; validation rejects oversize and unknown fields.
Mapping: each verdict against each band; BaselineInferred survives; stale item_fp dropped.

packages.title: Gate: replay and rig campaign with the exact baseline hidden
crates_files: vm/rig.ps1 (mode flag: hide the exact baseline)
packages.scope: Runs R3 and R4 of design 8.2 and checks S1 to S5 and W1 to W5 of design 8.3 and 8.4.
rules: The M1b gate criteria stay in force for the exact runs.
A flip (inferred-absent candidate whose key is in the truth baseline) fails the gate at count 1.
packages.acceptance: S1 flips = 0, danger_listed = 0, traps met, both VMs, merged and local. S4: L3 and L5 over the replay corpus. W2 >= 80% of the exact-only key candidates offered as Likely (below 50%: ship presence-only). W3 <= 1% recall cost. W5 reported for the host.

review_points.attack: Are the false-absent lists complete and honestly classified? Is any area marked that should not be? Do the leave-one-out pairs say anything about the host's case?

Find an A site that reaches Safe below Exact; find a P site used negated; plant or poison the cache or the shipped directory as a standard user; make the view claim Exact for a local file; break L5 with a fixture.

cut_or_move: S5 INF source: built only if gate M shows a need.
Automated release-build baseline packs: future maintenance.
The advisory model and the reader of advice: M6.
Lifting the cap per area (design 8.5): needs a user decision and at least three leave-one-out pairs.
open_questions: Q1 Unelevated runs without a cache: trust None with a warning (default), or an in-memory build each run?
Q2 Local-only level: presence-only unless an area passes S3 (default), or never any inferred absence?
Q3 Trust None still blocks from neighbours: accept that today's no-baseline plans gain Blocked items?
Q4 R4 needs a rig mode that hides the exact baseline; a drift test needs a Windows Update on a rig VM: wanted?
Q5 PURGE_KB_DIR: honoured only unelevated once the shipped directory must be admin-only?
Q6 Keep the later cap lift as an option, or rule it out?
